title: Nodes That Are Not Beaten From Above

concept.title: Carry the maximum of the road down with you
body: Call a node **good** if on the road from the root to the node there is no value larger than the value of the node (the root is always good). To decide this at a node, it is enough to know the **maximum value seen on the road so far**. Pass it down as an argument: a node is good when its value is at least that maximum, and the children get the larger of the old maximum and this node's value.

body.code:
def good(root, biggest):                     # biggest: the maximum on the road above
    if root is None:
        return 0
    count = 1 if root.val >= biggest else 0
    biggest = max(biggest, root.val)
    return count + good(root.left, biggest) + good(root.right, biggest)

# call: good(root, -infinity)

body: This is the same idea as the prefix in the previous problems: **information flows down** through an argument. Start with a number smaller than every possible value so that the root is counted.

statement: A node of a binary tree is good if no node on the road from the root to it (the node itself not counted) has a larger value than the node. The root is always good. Print the number of good nodes.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: Print the number of good nodes.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The good nodes are the root 3, then 4, then the 3 below the 1 (the road 3 1 3 has no larger value), and 5: four nodes.

hints: Pass the largest value of the road above the node down as an argument.
The node is good if its value is at least that largest value.
The children receive the larger of the old maximum and the value of the node.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))

    return 0

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

print(good(build_tree(vals), -10 ** 18))

explanation: Each call receives the maximum of the road above, counts the node when its value reaches that maximum, and passes the updated maximum to both children.
